cannot_be_concluded: Whether the recording is authentic, or whether it truthfully represents the events it appears to capture.
Whether any detected processing was performed with an intent to deceive; most processing (conversion, normalisation, noise gating, compression) is routine.
Whether the voice or content is synthetic/AI-generated: no test in this engine addresses speech synthesis.
That the file is unedited: the absence of indicators does not prove absence of editing. Crossfaded edits at matching levels, consistent backgrounds and re-recording can evade every test.
How many times the audio was lossily encoded (only the presence of at least one lossy generation is measurable).
Whether the audio was downsampled: downsampling leaves no trace distinguishable from a native recording at the lower rate.
Error rates on real casework: all performance figures come from a synthetic benchmark and are not real-world forensic accuracy.
false_positive_considerations: Digital silence is also produced by noise gates, 'silence removal' and recorder pause functions.
Level and spectral jumps occur naturally at speech and note onsets; they are reported only as supporting observations.
Clicks, plosives and percussive transients produce residual impulses similar to hard edits.
Loop-based music and synthetic signals repeat material legitimately.

findings.method: LPC residual impulse vs. neighbourhood maximum
findings.title: Isolated waveform discontinuity at 2.3000 s
findings.description: The prediction residual at sample 101429 is 6.4x larger than any residual value within 20 ms on either side; the waveform does not continue smoothly.
alternative_explanations: Click, pop, plosive or percussive onset in the original sound
Digital dropout, buffer underrun or bit error in the recording chain
A hard edit point (cut, insertion or gain step without crossfade)
limitations: Edits made at zero crossings with matching slope, or with crossfades, produce no impulse.

findings.method: exact-zero sample run detection
findings.title: Digital silence of 400 ms at 4.100-4.500 s
findings.description: 17640 consecutive samples are exactly zero in every channel, while the surrounding background noise is about -45 dBFS. A continuous acoustic recording would contain that background noise during pauses.
limitations: Dithered or noise-filled insertions are not exact zeros and are not detected by this test.

findings.method: log-mel self-similarity + waveform NCC verification
findings.title: Segment at 6.18-6.37 s duplicates 1.18-1.37 s
findings.description: 0.19 s of waveform at 6.184 s matches the waveform at 1.184 s with a normalised cross-correlation of 1.00000. Independently produced sounds do not repeat sample by sample.
alternative_explanations: Loop-based music production or sampled/repeated material
Synthetic or machine-generated signals with exact periodicity
Playback of the same recording twice within the scene
limitations: Copies that were re-filtered, time-stretched or mixed with other sound may fall below the NCC threshold.

findings.method: frame-wise hum phase tracking (absolute time reference)
findings.title: Mains-hum phase jumps by 2.13 rad near 2.32 s
findings.description: The 50 Hz hum phase changes by 2.13 rad (122 deg) around 2.32 s, while it evolves smoothly elsewhere. Removing or inserting samples breaks hum phase continuity.
alternative_explanations: Change of the electrical environment (another power circuit)
Strong interference near the hum frequency
limitations: Edits that remove an exact multiple of the hum period leave no phase step.
Time resolution about +/- 0.2 s because of the narrow band-pass filter.
